tasks.short: Select and arrange post-anesthesia medication or treatment

steps.what: Assess post-anesthesia symptoms, observations and treatment risks
Select a proposed post-anesthesia medication or treatment within local protocols
Enter the proposed post-anesthesia prescription and treatment instructions
Check and authorise the final post-anesthesia prescription and patient destination
Release the authorised post-anesthesia prescription to the care team
Explain the authorised regimen and monitor the patient's immediate response
outputs: explained post-anesthesia regimen and observed response

tasks.design: Test native post-anesthesia order fields in the clinical prescribing category {OTHER} to reuse already selected product and route details. Retain assessment, regimen selection and patient-specific entry, with the actual authorised prescriber checking the completed prescription before separate release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment must fit the recovering patient and actual prescribing authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Native order context can remove limited repeated fixed fields without choosing a regimen.
tasks.still_hard: Sedation, respiratory risk, interactions and deciding when escalation is required.
tasks.human_edge: Assess the patient's recovery and challenge an unsuitable proposed regimen.
tasks.altitude: Small entry relief; no expanded prescribing scope.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical order fields can reuse fixed details while local professional authority determines who prescribes and releases treatment.

assumptions: European scope varies; this graph uses an existing anesthesiologist-authorised pathway, not assumed independent nurse prescribing. Focal baseline is 90 share points; the anesthesiologist's 10 are counted outside it and fully retained. Shares are provisional.

The nurse produces observations in s1 and selects a proposal in s2 using current allergy/medication records and local protocols. s3 captures actual patient, product, regimen, timing and instructions. No free structured assessment or model clinical recommendation.

Test native context first. Only repeated selected product/route fields, 10% of s3, are removed. Clinical entry, repair and ordinary ungated draft save remain. Existing medication-surveillance runtime earns no saving.

s4 checks the complete exact prescription and destination after it exists; s5 releases only that authorised version. Edits void approval. Where the actual physician personally executes release, move s5 to that actor rather than giving the nurse unheld rights. Any additional response note must be separately counted or owned once in encounter documentation.
unknowns: Actual physician review and nurse entry time
research_questions: Does native context remove fixed-field typing without changing the prescriber's review?

already_counted.description: Patient-specific prescription entry and corrections remain in s3.
Actual prescriber verification remains outside focal labour.

incremental.description: Nurse checks native field defaults after protocol changes.

approvals.approved_version: s4 complete authorised post-anesthesia prescription, patient, regimen, timing and exact care-team destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=90; 20*0.10=2 share points removed gives 2.222 focal hours per 100, less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.722 net. Cautious case: a nonstandard regimen allows only 0.5 share points of product-field reuse, giving 0.055 net; prescriber work is fully retained and outside B.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform or evaluate diagnostic tests around anesthesia

steps.what: Perform the already authorised diagnostic test or obtain its original result
Enter or verify patient, test timing and original diagnostic result context
Locate the relevant radiograph, ECG or report for comparison
Evaluate diagnostic test results and recognise findings needing specialist review
Record the evaluated findings and limitations in the anesthesia record

tasks.design: Configure native patient-and-test-context links between diagnostic views in the clinical record and diagnostic-archive category {OTHER}. Shorten repeated result navigation while retaining test performance, identity/timing verification, clinical evaluation and original documentation; no model reads images or ECGs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant results may be spread across existing diagnostic views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native context links can reduce browsing without interpreting findings.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising clinically important changes and scope limits.
tasks.human_edge: Connect test findings with the patient's actual peri-anesthetic condition.
tasks.altitude: Less result navigation; no added diagnostic authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: patient-context links can shorten diagnostic-result retrieval while clinical interpretation remains a professional judgement.

assumptions: Boundary begins with an already authorised test; ordering or radiation authorisation is not hidden in the performance step. Nurse scope determines which tests are performed versus evaluated from an existing report. Shares are provisional.

The diagnostic service supplies original images, traces and reports with patient identifier, test type and timestamp; the nurse performs applicable tests in s1 and captures/checks context in s2. No free new device interface or structured interpretation is assumed.

Test native context links first. Only repeated diagnostic-view navigation, 20% of s3, is removed; patient/date matching and missing-result fallback remain. Existing device measurement runtime earns no saving.

Original finding entry and ordinary ungated save remain fully retained in s5. A separate specialist escalation send or new care order, if actually triggered, requires its own real first write and authorised release rather than being assumed automatic.
research_questions: Do native links preserve patient and test-date checks while removing browsing?

already_counted.description: Result matching and fallback remain in s3; clinical evaluation and original documentation remain in s4-s5.

incremental.description: Nurse checks result links after diagnostic-view changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 10*0.20=2 navigation hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5 net. Cautious case: an external radiograph requires manual archive matching, leaving 0.6 hours of existing-view navigation removed and 0.1 net; test performance and evaluation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select, order or administer pre-anesthetic medication

steps.what: Assess the patient and select a proposed pre-anesthetic medication regimen
Enter the proposed pre-anesthetic medication order
Check and authorise the complete medication order and administration destination
Release the authorised pre-anesthetic medication order for administration
Check administration rights and administer the authorised pre-anesthetic medication
Record actual medication, dose, time and patient response

tasks.design: Test native protocol favourites in the clinical prescribing category {OTHER} to reuse fixed product and route fields in a proposed pre-anesthetic order. The actual prescriber checks the completed order before release; the nurse retains patient-specific checks, physical administration and the separate original administration record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication selection and administration must match the patient's risks and actual authorisation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native favourites remove limited fixed-field typing without choosing or administering medicine.
tasks.still_hard: Allergies, fasting status, interactions, respiratory risk and changing clinical state.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an authorised order should be withheld and escalated.
tasks.altitude: Less fixed order entry; unchanged administration and scope obligations.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native protocol favourites can reuse fixed medication fields, while prescriber authority and administration checks remain with qualified staff.

assumptions: This is an existing anesthesiologist-authorised European pathway. Focal B=90; the prescriber's 10 share points are outside it, fully retained. Independent nurse prescribing is not assumed; shares are provisional.

The nurse obtains assessment and current medication/allergy facts in s1 and enters actual patient, regimen, timing and instructions in s2. Native favourites supply only approved fixed fields. Missing or inappropriate defaults are corrected in retained s2 and checked in s3. No free structured assessment or new surveillance saving.

Only fixed product/route entry, 15% of s2, is removed. s3 checks the completed exact order before release s4 and administration s5; any change voids approval. s5 includes immediate patient, medicine, dose, route, timing and condition checks and withholding when unsafe.

s6 occurs only after actual administration and records the observed dose/time/response, not the planned order. Ordinary author record saving is retained and ungated. Where the prescriber must execute the release, assign s4 to that actual role rather than inventing nurse rights.
research_questions: Do native favourites remove fixed typing without increasing wrong-default correction?

already_counted.description: Order entry repair and original administration documentation remain.
Prescriber review remains outside focal labour.

incremental.description: Nurse checks favourites after protocol changes.

approvals.approved_version: s3 complete authorised order, exact patient, regimen, timing and administration destination; edits void approval
s3 complete authorised order for the exact patient, medicine, dose, route and time, conditional on immediate administration checks in s5; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=90; 20*0.15=3 share points removed gives 3.333 focal hours per 100, less 0.7 upkeep gives 2.633 net. Cautious case: unusual premedication needs manual fields, leaving 0.7 share points of supported reuse, giving 0.077 net. Prescriber and physical administration work stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess post-anesthesia recovery and readiness against discharge criteria
Write the discharge assessment, destination and patient instructions
Review the completed discharge plan and authorise the exact patient destination
outputs: authorised final discharge plan and destination

steps.what: Activate the authorised post-anesthesia discharge to the checked destination
inputs: authorised final discharge plan and destination

steps.what: Explain the authorised discharge instructions and hand over the patient
inputs: authorised final discharge plan and destination
outputs: explained instructions and completed patient handover

tasks.design: Use native patient/procedure context in the anesthesia-record category {OTHER} to avoid repeated discharge-header entry. Retain recovery assessment, personalised instruction writing, actual discharge authorisation and patient handover; activate only the completed authorised destination and plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readiness depends on the patient's current recovery and actual local discharge authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record context can remove repeated headers without deciding readiness.
tasks.still_hard: Unstable recovery, appropriate destination, escort arrangements and patient understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a patient who meets numbers but is not ready to leave care.
tasks.altitude: Small documentation relief; no expanded discharge authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native patient/procedure fields can reduce repeated discharge headers while readiness assessment and authorisation remain clinical work.

assumptions: This graph uses a local pathway with anesthesiologist discharge authorisation, not assumed independent nurse rights. Focal B=80; other-role review20 remains fully retained outside it. Shares are provisional.

The nurse produces actual recovery observations in s1 and writes assessment, instructions and destination in s2. Existing records supply patient/procedure identifiers only. No free scored assessment or automatic discharge recommendation is assumed.

Test native context first. Only repeated identity/procedure headers, 8% of s2, are removed; actual observations, instructions, correction and ordinary ungated draft saving remain. Missing context is repaired in retained s2.

s3 reviews the completed exact plan and destination before s4 activates discharge; any clinical or destination change voids authorisation. s5 explains and physically hands over that authorised plan without a separate unpriced message send. If a separate written packet is actually sent, add its own release step and time.
unknowns: Whether separate packet sending is required
research_questions: Can native context remove repeated headers while preserving readiness and destination checks?

already_counted.description: Original assessment/instruction writing and corrections remain in s2.
Actual clinical discharge review remains outside focal labour.

incremental.description: Nurse checks discharge fields after pathway changes.

approvals.approved_version: s3 complete authorised discharge plan, exact patient, instructions and destination; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=80; 25*0.08=2 share points removed gives 2.5 focal hours per 100, less 0.5 upkeep gives 2 net. Cautious case: an unusual destination needs custom headers, leaving 0.5 share points of reuse, giving 0.125 net; readiness, prescriber review and handover remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native field reuse and diagnostic links reduce small entry/navigation costs; actual clinical scope, prescriber authorisation and direct care stay intact.
skills_to_grow: Recognise local scope and release rights
role.ambitious_version: No autonomous prescribing, diagnosis or discharge is proposed.
